subclass: Balanced Continuous Resource-Hour Allocation / Transportation-Style Assignment
reference: Classical balanced transportation and minimum-cost allocation models
math_formula:
### Mathematical Model
Let I be people/resources and J be projects/requests. Person i has available hours S_i. Project j requires D_j hours. Assigning one hour from i to j has cost c_{i,j}, and person i can contribute at most u_{i,j} hours to project j.

Decision variable:
- x_{i,j} >= 0: continuous hours assigned from person i to project j.

Objective:
minimize sum_{i in I} sum_{j in J} c_{i,j} x_{i,j}.

Constraints:
- sum_{j in J} x_{i,j} = S_i for every person i.
- sum_{i in I} x_{i,j} = D_j for every project j.
- 0 <= x_{i,j} <= u_{i,j} for every person-project pair.

This is not a binary one-to-one assignment model. The variables are continuous assigned hours.
natural_language_example: A service operations team must allocate available specialist hours to project requests. Each specialist has a fixed number of available hours, each project has a required number of hours, each specialist-project pair has an hourly cost, and every pair has a listed maximum allowed contribution. Total available hours equal total required hours. The goal is to assign continuous hours to minimize total assignment cost while fully using all available hours, exactly satisfying every project's required hours, and respecting every contribution limit.
local_modification_notes: Internal OR-CPT version uses a latent feasible allocation to guarantee total supply equals total demand, exposes the complete cost and contribution-limit matrices, and forbids binary one-to-one matching, inequality relaxation of supply/demand balances, and omitted pairwise upper bounds.
